verdict.rationale: Otter's own MCP Server is described as OAuth-authenticated with granular permissions, and the assistant can only access meetings the user explicitly authorizes. That is a scoped, least-privilege grant for an agent, but it rests on a single blog line. The Public API is documented only as API-key auth, with no mention of scopes, key restriction, or per-agent issuance. missing for 10: documented scope definitions or permission granularity, scoped/restricted Public API keys, credential issuance, rotation and revocation management, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: OAuth-authenticated with granular permissions. Your AI assistant can only access meetings you explicitly authorize
base URL https://api.otter.ai/v1 with API-key auth
